title: Recoil transport and environmental exposure of black-hole merger remnants
abstract: Black-hole mergers in stellar clusters leave remnants whose recoil carries them through environments of different density and composition. Their availability for subsequent interactions depends on residence in those environments, as well as on gravitational retention. We study when continuous drift and diffusion preserve finite-time residence under discrete gravitational encounters. Published multimass distributions for six Galactic clusters supply consistent potentials, species distributions and local scattering backgrounds. Collisionless controls connect these inputs to orbital occupation, while a conditional Omega Centauri calculation compares finite encounters with a diffusion process having the same local velocity-change moments. A backward occupation equation relates their mean-residence difference to a nonlocal generator residual. We test a first-response approximation through complete-transition replacements, with predictions recorded before independent mixture trajectories are generated. The numerical endpoint distributions differ, but the response test remains limited by sampling precision, refinement uncertainty and numerical-boundary continuation. It therefore does not establish or reject the proposed prediction accuracy. An exploratory covariance-factor diagnostic identifies a discontinuity that can weaken shared-noise coupling while preserving each marginal diffusion law; its effect on trajectory-estimator efficiency remains to be tested. The calculations distinguish exact response identities, measurable encounter effects and the numerical precision required for an observable-specific transport criterion. They remain conditional on the adopted hosts and encounter prescription, without a calibrated cluster residence or merger-rate prediction.
